title: Salt-tolerant rice for delta agriculture
bottleneck: Sea-level rise is salinizing the great river deltas — the Mekong, Ganges-Brahmaputra, Nile — where hundreds of millions grow rice, but salt-tolerant varieties yield 20-40 percent less than elite cultivars and tolerance breaks down under combined salinity, submergence, and heat. Breeding has produced incremental gains, yet the rate of salinization from sea-level rise and groundwater extraction outpaces varietal improvement. No variety sustains commercial yields at the salinities projected for 2050 deltas.
why_it_blocks: Delta rice feeds a significant fraction of humanity; losing it means food insecurity and mass migration from the world's most densely populated regions. The breeding shortfall turns a solvable agronomic problem into a humanitarian one.
current_state: Marker-assisted breeding has released moderately tolerant varieties now planted across millions of hectares in Bangladesh and Vietnam. But these buy time rather than solving the problem, and investment in next-generation tolerance remains small relative to the stakes.
